source: docs/framework-research/09-hiring-workflows-draft.md §1, revision 2, approved by the owner 2026-11-08. Company perspective only; the candidate perspective is not shown to employer-side participants.
intro: This is a draft of how a hire runs, from the first sign that a role is needed to the lessons captured when the requisition closes. It is not how your organisation does it; it is our best picture, and you are asked to correct it.
prompts: Walk along it from C-01. Where does it match how a hire actually runs where you work, and where does it not?
Which step is missing? Which two are really one step?
Who owns C-06, writing the role and its requirements, and C-07, the sign-off, in your organisation?
Where do holds actually happen in this picture, and what brings one back?
At C-12 to C-14, who decides? Does the hiring manager cut people from the slate before interviewing?
Is there anything on this chart you would not want a candidate to see?

nodes.name: Need identified
nodes.summary: Trigger: attrition, growth, new scope, backfill. Often undocumented; C-02 is the first record.

nodes.name: Manpower request submitted
nodes.summary: Business case: why, what level, cost, when, backfill or new headcount.

nodes.name: Request review
nodes.owner: Committee: finance, HR or people partner, the HM's manager, department head
nodes.summary: Checks budget, headcount plan, alternatives (redistribute, contractor, automate).

nodes.name: Approval decision
nodes.owner: Budget owner, on the committee's recommendation
nodes.summary: Approved, rejected with a reason, or deferred with a resubmission date. A deferral past its date unreviewed escalates.

nodes.name: HR role-definition template
nodes.summary: Standing artefact: required fields, structure, requirement types, weight scale, evidence-standard slots, comp band and level. HR owns the structure, refreshed rarely.

nodes.name: HM drafts role definition and structured requirements
nodes.owner: Hiring manager, solely responsible for content
nodes.summary: Approved request plus the template become a role document: purpose, outcomes, typed and weighted requirements, alternatives, thresholds, evidence standards, level, comp band, location, working conditions.

nodes.name: Conformance and comp check
nodes.summary: Conforms, non-conforming back to C-06 with the field list, or hold with a revisit date. HR does not re-judge the substance of the requirements.

nodes.name: Job description rendered and posted
nodes.owner: Recruiter renders; HM approves the text
nodes.summary: The posting is a rendering of C-06, never the source of truth.

nodes.name: Applications received or sourced
nodes.summary: Applications, referrals and outreach form the applicant pool.

nodes.name: Knockout and compliance filter
nodes.owner: ATS rules set by the recruiter
nodes.summary: Hard constraints only: authorisation, location, licence. Keyword knockouts live here today, the first source of false negatives.

nodes.name: Initial screen via match record
nodes.owner: Recruiter or HR screener using the system
nodes.summary: Evidence gathered per candidate (C-11a), requirements judged against it with three coverage numbers (C-11b), and a system-driven clarification round for unresolved items (C-11c).

nodes.name: Screen decision
nodes.owner: Recruiter, using the match record; HM may audit or override
nodes.summary: Advance, reject, hold with a revisit date, or needs HM input on flagged judgments.

nodes.name: Recruiter screen call, with remaining clarifications
nodes.summary: Interest, logistics, comp, constraints. The recruiter asks the still-unresolved items live from system-generated questions and records the structured answers.

nodes.name: Slate to HM
nodes.summary: Accept the slate, reject individuals (each recorded as an override), or reject the slate back to sourcing or to the role definition. Open question: do hiring managers cut individuals before interviewing often enough for this to be a decision point?

nodes.name: Interviews
nodes.summary: Interview evidence and working-style indicators. Interviews target unresolved and met-via-equivalency items first.

nodes.name: Assessment or work sample (optional)
nodes.summary: Additional evidence items.

nodes.name: Hire decision
nodes.summary: Select, reject all and re-source, reject all and redefine, or defer with a revisit date. Recorded against the match record so the outcome links to screening.

nodes.name: Offer prepared
nodes.owner: HR and comp with the HM
nodes.summary: Off-band offers loop to the budget owner.

nodes.name: Offer outcome
nodes.summary: Accepted, negotiation, declined, or no response by a date, which is treated as declined and escalated to the recruiting lead.

nodes.name: Notify non-selected
nodes.summary: Rejection with a substantive reason where policy allows. The match record makes a substantive reason cheap.

nodes.name: Pre-boarding
nodes.summary: Checks, paperwork, equipment. Verification of self-attested evidence belongs here if not earlier; a failed check goes back to C-17 or to withdrawal.

nodes.name: Start and onboarding
nodes.summary: Employee in role.

nodes.name: 30-day check-in
nodes.summary: Fit rating, both directions. An outcome link.

nodes.name: 90-day review
nodes.summary: Fit and performance: confirm, extend probation, or exit. An outcome link.

nodes.name: Retention and performance at 6 to 12 months
nodes.summary: Outcome data that feeds calibration.

nodes.name: Requisition closed; lessons captured
nodes.summary: Metrics, overrides and hold history become the process record.
